dedupe_keys.name: scenarios of technical and useful ground source heat pump potential for building heating and cooling in western switzerland

description: This data set estimates the technical and useful potential of shallow ground-source heat pumps for building heating and cooling in Western Switzerland. It was published by Alina Walch, Xiang Li and Jonathan Chambers with an article in the journal Energy. Technical potential is the most heat that dense vertical closed-loop borehole systems, 50 to 200 metres deep, could extract without over-exploiting the ground; useful potential is what could reach building heating and cooling through water-to-water heat pumps. Files hold available area, heating and cooling demand and the resulting potentials for future scenarios of cooling demand (200 Monte Carlo runs) and climate change, with and without district heating and cooling networks, whose zones are included. Coverage is about 80,000 parcels in the Cantons of Vaud and Geneva, excluding the Alps and the Jura, at 400 by 400 metre pixels or by network zone. Files are CSV tables, a GeoPackage and a Data Package JSON on Zenodo under CC-BY-4.0 at no cost. Caveats: results come from the paper's models and assumptions, and methods are in the articles and the PDF documentation. Simulation uses are heat pump and thermal network planning under climate scenarios. Related records: none linked on the provider's pages read on the day.
